strategy.rationale: Step 0 with only 12 initial data points in a 2D space and a large batch size of 16. The yield landscape is highly skewed (median 0.3, max 73) suggesting a sharp peak region. Thompson sampling is ideal here: (1) batch size 16 > 10 makes it computationally efficient and naturally diverse, (2) no budget constraint allows balanced exploration/exploitation, (3) with sparse data, Thompson's stochastic sampling will spread points across both the promising high-yield region near the best observation and underexplored areas, building a much better surrogate for subsequent steps. Matern-2.5 handles the peaked but smooth yield surface well. Low noise floor lets the GP learn noise freely from the data.
